description: Conversion of single dwelling house to 2x self-contained dwelling houses including part single storey, part two storey rear extension, two storey side extension and associated refuse storage.
decision_conditions: The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved refuse storage details as set out in drawings JN15-02-04-26-F1 V1 and JN15-02-04-26-C1 V2 before the development is occupied. The refuse storage shall be retained and maintained as such for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure the provision of refuse storage in accordance with the London Borough of Enfield - Waste and Recycling Planning Storage Guidance 2024

The development hereby approved shall be carried out in full accordance with the Energy Statement prepared by LHP, unless otherwise submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The approved measures for reducing carbon emissions and improving energy efficiency, including but not limited to the use of low and zero carbon technologies, enhanced building fabric performance, and energy-efficient systems, shall be fully implemented prior to first occupation of the development and retained thereafter.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

Following practical completion of works a final Energy Performance Certificate with accompanying Building Regulations compliance report shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Where applicable, a Display Energy Certificate shall be submitted within 18 months following first occupation.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP20 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policies DMD49, DMD50 and DMD51 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The development shall not commence until details of source control SuDS have been submitted to and approved by the Local Authority. Source control SuDS measures include green roofs, rain gardens and permeable paving. The details must include plans, specifications and maintenance information. The developer should use the SuDS Proforma for minor developers found on our webpage https://www.enfield.gov.uk/services/planning/sustainable-drainage-systems to assist them through our requirements.Reason: To ensure the sustainable management of water, minimise flood risk, minimise discharge of surface water outside of the curtilage of the property and ensure that the drainage system will remain functional throughout the lifetime of the development in accordance with Policy CP28 of the Core Strategy, DMD Policy 61, and Policies SI12 & SI13 of the London Plan and the NPPF and to maximise opportunities for sustainable development, improve water quality, biodiversity, local amenity and recreation value.

Notwithstanding the provisions of the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015 or any amending Order, no buildings or extensions to buildings shall be erected without the prior approval in writing of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: In order to prevent overdevelopment of the site and to safeguard the character and appearance of the area and the amenities of neighbouring occupiers.

Prior to the first occupation of either dwelling hereby approved, the vehicle parking space for the retained 3-bedroom dwelling shown on revised drawings JN15-02-04-26-F1 and JN15-02-04-26-C1 shall be provided and made available for use. The parking space shall thereafter be retained for vehicle parking purposes and shall not be used for any other purpose without the prior written consent of the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure satisfactory off-street parking provision and in the interests of highway safety in accordance with Policies T6 and T6.1 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies DMD45 and DMD47 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).[

Prior to the first occupation of either dwelling hereby approved, the existing vehicle crossover serving the site shall be permanently discontinued and the associated footway, kerb and verge reinstated to the satisfaction of the Local Highway Authority in accordance with details to be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To ensure that the development does not result in the unnecessary loss of on-street parking capacity and in the interests of highway and pedestrian safety, in accordance with Policies T2, T3 and T6 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies DMD45 and DMD47 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014).

The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice.Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans: JN15-02-04-26-B1JN15-02-04-26-A1JN15-02-04-26-E1JN15-02-04-26-D1LHP-15AR-BS-02LHP-15AR-CS-01  JN15-02-04-26-F1 V1  JN15-02-04-26-C1 V2  Sustainable Drainage  Energy Statement   Highway Impact Pro Forma Reason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

Unless otherwise specified in the application the materials to be used for the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted along with work of making good shall be carried out in materials to match those of the existing building.   Reason: To ensure that the appearance of the development respects the appearance, existing materials and built and natural features of the surrounding area.

No above ground works shall commence until details of a landscaping plan detailing trees, shrubs and grass to be planted and the treatment of any hard surfaced amenity areas has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The approved landscaping shall be implemented prior to first occupation of either dwelling, or during the first planting season following occupation where planting cannot reasonably take place beforehand.Reason: To provide a satisfactory appearance

The development shall be designed and constructed to ensure that the internal consumption of potable water does not exceed 105 litres per person per day. This shall be achieved through the installation of water-efficient fittings, appliances, and, where applicable, water recycling systems. The development shall be maintained in accordance with these measures for the lifetime of the development.Reason: In the interest of sustainable development and to ensure that the Local Planning Authority may be satisfied that CO2 emission reduction targets are met in accordance with Policy CP21 of the Enfield Core Strategy (2010), Policy DMD58 of the Enfield Development Management Document (2014)

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the cycle parking details as set out in drawings JN15-02-04-26-F1 V1 and JN15-02-04-26-C1 V2 before the development is occupied. The cycle parking shall be retained and maintained as such for the lifetime of the development.Reason: To ensure the provision of cycle parking in accordance with Policy T6.1 of the London Plan (2021), the Council's adopted standards and London Cycling Design Standards Chapter 8
